title: AI Receptionist for Plumbers: Worth It, or Just Answer the Damn Phone?
meta: Is an AI receptionist worth it for a plumbing business? The honest math vs. missed-call text-back, a live answering service, and just picking up. Real owner quotes.
dek: Some SaaS bro in a vest sold you a robot that answers your phone like it's hosting a podcast. Before you hand your livelihood to a chatbot, here's the honest math.
verdict_text: For most one- and two-truck shops, an AI receptionist is a $300-a-month answer to a $30 fucking problem. Catch your calls first. Buy the robot last — if ever.

blocks.h: You're bleeding jobs you already paid for
blocks.html:
A plumber who can't answer the phone loses work. One owner on a two-man crew counted 47 missed calls in 30 days — nobody's free to pick up when you're both under a sink. Every one is a homeowner who said "fuck it" and called the next guy.

That part's real. Where it turns to bullshit is what people sell you to fix it.

blocks.h: The stat every vendor quotes, and nobody can source
blocks.intro_html: You'll see this on every AI-phone landing page on Earth. We went looking for where it came from:
blocks.label: Unverified
blocks.claim: "85% of callers who hit voicemail never call back."
blocks.small: One vendor credits Forbes. Another PATLive. A third an outfit called Aira. Every one points at a different source and the trail dead-ends. Probably directionally true — but anyone quoting it to the decimal is blowing smoke up your ass to sell a subscription.
blocks.outro_html: A number you can trust, from a real survey: 41% hang up after 1–2 minutes on hold, and 21% immediately dial a competitor. — CallRail 2025 You just need to answer the fucking phone.

notes.text: Anything that grabs the name and number and texts it to me works. I'll call back in five minutes. I don't need it to book anything.
I'd avoid a business that uses an AI receptionist. The second I realize I'm talking to a bot, I hang up.

rows.note: A booked job's worth $300–800. Miss it, it's the next plumber's. If you can pick up — pick up, you cheap bastard.
Auto-text fires back while you're under a sink. ~80% of the value for 5% of the cost. For most shops, the whole answer.
Real judgment, won't hallucinate a 2 a.m. appointment. Worth it once you're missing genuine after-hours jobs.
Fine for 'are you open.' Shits the bed on anything weird — and plumbing is 90% weird. Not your front line.

blocks.intro_html: Missing 5+ real-job calls a week? You're leaving $1,000+/mo on the floor. Fix it in this order:
steps: Turn on missed-call text-back ($30). Today. It kills most of the problem.
Add a live human service once you're missing real after-hours money.
Consider AI dead last, overflow only — test it on your own weird-ass calls first.
blocks.outro_html: Don't drop $200 on a robot to fix what a $30 text already handles.

workorder.h: We'll wire up your whole call-capture stack
workorder.p: Missed-call text-back, booking, follow-up — set up and working, so no call turns into a job for some other asshole. No monthly games.

faq.q: Is an AI receptionist worth it for a small plumbing business?
faq.a: For most one- or two-truck shops, no — not first. Missed-call text-back (~$30/mo) recovers most of the lost calls for a fraction of the cost. AI makes sense later, for after-hours overflow only.

faq.q: What's the cheapest way to stop missing calls?
faq.a: Missed-call text-back: when a call goes unanswered, an automatic text fires to the caller. It runs about $30/month and catches roughly 80% of the value of a full answering service.
